units.function: Route tests for Issue attachment upload/content delivery, global/company size caps, MIME inference, byte ranges, tenant/Issue authorization and attachment-backed artifact metadata canonicalization.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest -> Issue routes -> mocked access/Issue/company/work-product/activity services and in-memory StorageService; object metadata and blob operations are not transactional.
units.keyDataModels: Attachment metadata with tenant/Issue/object key/MIME/size/SHA/creator, company upload cap, byte range and Work Product artifact metadata referencing an attachment.
units.lifecycle: Authorize parent Work -> buffer upload -> classify mostly from declared MIME/filename -> store blob -> create attachment metadata -> serve inline/download/range -> derive canonical artifact paths; deletion/retention lifecycle is not covered.
units.testAssessment: The sandbox passed 1 pure test and failed 20 route tests on TCP bind; approved unsandboxed run passed 21/21. HTTP/range and reference checks are useful, but arbitrary active content is explicitly accepted and storage consistency, scanning, deletion and evidence governance are absent.
units.designRationale: Support broad user artifacts and media previews while limiting size, hiding cross-tenant existence, enforcing parent-Work access and preventing clients from injecting artifact URLs.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS attachments may contain enterprise data and responsibility evidence, requiring verified classification, quarantine, immutable provenance, retention, residency and controlled egress in addition to ordinary upload/download behavior.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind DataStore/Evidence/Blob ports. Retain min(global, tenant) limits, range semantics, cross-tenant 404, parent-resource authorization and server-derived canonical references. Require streaming upload, magic-byte/type policy, malware/archive scanning and quarantine, isolated active-content origin, safe filenames, checksums, encryption, transactional metadata/outbox, legal hold/retention, access receipts and Agent Run/accountable-human provenance.
units.responsibilityConflict: A fixture SHA and mutable attachment reference are insufficient evidence. Arbitrary executables and potentially inline active content can enter the control plane without a data-authorization contract, scanner result or accountable acceptance decision.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL active-content policy gap: arbitrary executable MIME is accepted and HTML may lack forced attachment disposition. HIGH classification gap: filename/MIME inference lacks byte verification and malware/archive scanning. HIGH consistency gap: blob/metadata transaction and orphan cleanup are untested. HIGH evidence-governance gap: checksum, immutability, legal hold and provenance are absent. MEDIUM resource gap: upload is buffered and concurrency limits are untested. MEDIUM filename/inline gap: header injection, SVG and isolated origin are absent. MEDIUM authorization gap: Agent/Run/scoped sharing paths are untested.
